correctness.rationale: Upper bound: every closed translate missing y violates at least one facet and is contained in the corresponding strict projection halfspace. Lower bound: for j and cutoff a in projection support range, shifted T_j,a=a*u_j+t(K-p_j) has its j-th face at a and all other inequalities slack on support because tη≥2R, so its mass agrees with that halfspace and it misses y when a<u_j·y. Sup over increasing strict cutoffs gives exact measure even with atoms. Upper quantiles are well defined/finite for α>0 and closed ray mass upper semicontinuity yields displayed polyhedral contour. For boxes, other coordinate support widths are coverable iff tℓ_i≥w_i; both opposing facet cuts realize coordinate halfspaces. For t below max w_i/ℓ_i, uniform measure on a support segment parallel to failing coordinate with query y beyond max(L,w/2) gives excluded halfspace mass >L/w while every missing translate captures ≤L/w. All-point, all-law finite equality is proved analytically; 9,342 exact rational witness tests in inspected verifier cannot certify universal quantifiers.

final_claim: For an irredundantly faceted full-dimensional compact polytope K in R^d, chosen relative-interior facet points p_j with clearance η>0, a compact supported probability μ in a ball of radius R, and t>0 with tη≥2R, the translated-tK depth equals min_j μ{u_j·x≥u_j·y} for every y including atomic laws; all positive depth-level sets are the facet normal upper-quantile halfspace intersection. For axis-aligned boxes K of side lengths ℓ_i and supports in a box of widths w_i, the least universal t is max_i w_i/ℓ_i.
